full_judgment:
Bijan Kumar Das, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause why the proceeding in Family Court Suit No. 52 of 1993 now pending before the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge and Family Court. Dhaka shall not be withdrawn and transferred to the Court of the Assistant Judge, Sader and Family Court, Faridpur for disposal. 

 2. The short fact leading to this Rule is that the opposite party filed Family Suit No. 52 of 1993 in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka against the present-petitioner praying for declaration that he is entitled to the guardianship of the person of the minors under Section 7 of the Guardians & Wards Act. 1890 stating, inter alia that he is the father of the minor sons, namely. Khondoker Ehasn Elahi (Allen) and Khondoker Monzur Elahi (Alex) aged 14 years and 10 years respectively. It has been stated that the present petitioner was divorced on 22.2.1993 and since before the divorce the present petitioner was residing in her paternal house with the said minors under the care of her brother. It has also been alleged that present-opposite party having properties in Dhaka is a permanent resident of Dhaka and works in the Ministry of Agriculture. In the petition before the Family Court it has also been stated that the mother (present petitioner) of the minor has no source of income and she is not capable of maintaining the minor sons and unless the minor sons are reared up under the guardianship of the present opposite party they shall be deprived of all facilities including their education. In the petition it has been claimed that the petitioner-fathers the legal guardian of the minor sons and he is entitled to be declared as guardian of the person of the minor sons. 

 3. The present petitioner being the opposite party entered appearance before the Family Court on 28.2.1994 and filed an application under section 6(1)(a)(b) of the Family Court Ordinance 1985 which was rejected by the learned Judge of the Family Court on 16.4.1994 on the ground that since the petitioner resident within the territorial jurisdiction of the Family Court in Dhaka the suit before the Family Court in Dhaka is maintainable. Against the said order Miscellaneous Appeal No. 120 of 1994 was filed before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which on transfer, was heard and dismissed by the 4th Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on 13.9.1996 upholding the order of the Family Court. The present petitioner thereafter moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. Shamin Khaled Ahmed the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the cause title of the miscellaneous application has been wrongly described to be one under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure due to inadvertence. According to the learned Advocate this miscellaneous application should be read as one under section 25 of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 and the statements made in the application would clearly indicate that for all purpose the ingredients of section 25 of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 are attracted and the name is not one under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 6. We have perused the miscellaneous application carefully and we find that though in the cause title it has been maintained to be on application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the facts disclosed in the application show that the application is one under section 25 of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985. We accordingly, treat this application as one under section 25 of the Family Court Ordinance. 1985. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that Family Court Suit No. 52 of 1993 before the Assistant Judge 3rd Court and Family Court. Dhaka was filed under Guardians and Wards Act 1890 and in the prayer also the petitioner preyed for declaration of Guardianship of the persons of the minors under section 7 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. The learned Advocate submits that the above suit before the Family Court indicates that the case was filed under section 9 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. According to the learned Advocate the suit was filed before the Family Court as section 24 of the Family Court Ordinance. 1985 provides that "A Family Court shall be deemed to be a District Court for the purpose of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (VIII of 1890) and notwithstanding anything contained in this Ordinance shall, in dealing with matters specified in that Act, follow the procedure specified in that Act, "From a reading of this provision it appears that the procedure laid down in the Guardians and Wards Act. 1890 shall be applicable in dealing with the matters in respect of appointment or declaration of a guardian of the person of a minor under the Family Courts Ordinance. 1985. A special Bench of this Division to which one of us (Mahmudul Amin Choudhury. J) was the presiding Judge held in the case of Pochon Rishi Dasi Vs. Khuku Rani Dasi and others reported in 17BLD 563 that 

 "Farther for appointment of guardians the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 is still in force which is applicable to all the citizens of the country and the District Judge was competent to deal with the matters acting as a District Court but now after coming into force of Family Court Ordinance the forum i.e. the District Court has been changed. Section 24 of the Ordinance provides that a Family Court shall be deemed to be a District Court for the purposes of Guardians and Wards Act and it has further provided that in dealing the matter specified in that Act the Family Court shall follow the Special provisions of that Act and the District Judge has now been made the appellate Court who shall follow the provision of section 17." 

 "This indicates that when any person intended to get an order passed under Guardian and Wards Act he should approach the Family Court as that Court has been given the exclusive jurisdiction to deal with the cases filed under that Act and this has been made a District Court under that Act." 

 8. In view of the aforesaid proposition of law as laid down above it is held that for the purpose of declaration or appointment of any person as guardian of the minor, the provisions of Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 shall apply. The cause title of the suit before the Family Court would show that it was filed under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890 and the relief in the prayer has been sought for under section 7 of the said Act. Section 7 of Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 provides the power of the Court to make order as to Guardianship and section 9 of the said Act empowers the Court with jurisdiction to entertain an application for appointment of Guardian. Section 9(1) of the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 runs as follows:- 

 "If the application is with respect to the guardianship of the person of the minor, it shall be made to the District Court having jurisdiction in the place where the minor ordinarily resides." 

 9. In the present matter admittedly the minors have been residing at Faridpur with their mother (the present petitioner) under the care of her brother. According to the case made out in the petition for appointment of Guardian it appears to us that the present opposite party as the father of the minor sons in claiming guardianship of the persons of the minor sons, who ordinarily reside within the jurisdiction of the Family Court in Faridpur. In the cause title also the present petitioner has been described as a resident of College Road, near C & B. Colony, within the police station and District Faridpur and the minor sons reside with their mother as specifically asserted in paragraph No. 4 of the application filed before the Family Court in Dhaka. In view of the legal position as indicated above and in view of the admitted fact that the minor sons ordinarily reside within the jurisdiction of the Family Court in Faridpur we are of the opinion that the Family Court in the present matter which shall be deemed to be District Court for the purpose of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 is the Family Court in Faridpur and not the Family Court in Dhaka where the present suit had been filed. The Family Court in Dhaka has no jurisdiction to entertain the present suit in as much as it in the Family Court in Faridpur who has to exclusive jurisdiction to entertain the application for appointment of guardian as admittedly the minor boys ordinarily reside within the jurisdiction of the Family Court in Faridpur. 

 10. We therefore, find substance in the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the present suit is not entertain able by the 3rd Court of the Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka for lack of jurisdiction. Should then we dismiss the Family Suit filed in the Family Court in Dhaka having no jurisdiction to entertain the suit? Our answer is of course, No. And this is also not the prayer of the petitioner before us. 

 11. In view of the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner we have already held that this Miscellaneous application shall he treated as one filed under section 25 of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 Section 25 of the Family Courts Ordinance 1985 runs as follows:- 

 "(1) The High Court Division may either on application of any party or of its own accord by an order in writing- 

 (a) transfer any suit under this Ordinance from one Family Court to another Family Court in the same district or from a Family Court of one district to a Family Court of another district." 

 From a perusal of the above provision it is clear to us that this Division is competent to transfer any suit under this Ordinance from a Family Court of one district to a Family Court of another district on the application of either party or of its own accord. In the case before us, the present petitioner prayed for transfer of the suit from the Family Court of Dhaka to any Family Court in the district of Faridpur. We have already held that the Family Court in, the district Faridpur has exclusive jurisdiction to entertain the suit for appointment of the present opposite party as the guardian of the persons of his minor sons. Accordingly we hold that the instant Family Court Suit No. 52 of 1993 now pending in the Third Court of Assistant Judge and Family Court Dhaka should be withdrawn from the said court and be transferred to any Family Court in the district Faridpur for disposal in accordance with law. 

 12. In the result, this rule is made absolute. The Family Court Suit No. 52 of 1993 be withdrawn from the 310 Court of Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka and be transferred to the Court of the Assistant Judge and Family Court in Faridpur. It is directed that if there are more then one Family Court in Faridpur the Senior most Family Court shall try the present suit. It is also directed that suit may be disposed of expeditiously.
